__inputs.label: Gateway job name (app.kubernetes.io/instance by default)
__inputs.description: The name of the gateway to monitor

description: Per-stage request lifecycle latency for Conduktor Gateway (ADR-0015).

options.content:
**Request lifecycle latency** — one panel per T0→T10 stage from ADR-0015. Requires the gateway feature flag `GATEWAY_FEATURE_FLAGS_LIFECYCLE_METRICS=true`; with it off, panels are empty.

**Reading gaps (ADR §7):** a missing/zero series means traffic didn't reach that stage, not that instrumentation is broken. Cache hits skip `upstreamwait`/rebuilder (healthy); `acks=0` produce skips `total`; a ~30s `total` spike with no `upstreamwait` is an upstream timeout.

**Percentiles (ADR §4):** buckets start at 1ms, so P99 reads flat for the sub-ms stages until they degrade; use mean and max for those, P99 for `upstreamwait`.

panels.description: Full-pipeline latency (gateway.request.total.duration). Mean and max are exact at any magnitude; P99 is meaningful once the pipeline crosses ~1ms. A ~30s spike with no upstreamwait count is an upstream timeout (ADR §7 #6).
panels.title: Total request latency (T0→T10)

panels.description: Stacked mean latency per lifecycle stage — the dominant band is the bottleneck. Interceptor stages are per-invocation means (their _count is interceptors run, not requests, ADR §1); use the Interceptors section for per-interceptor attribution.
panels.title: Where the time goes (mean per stage)

panels.description: Recording rate per stage. A missing/zero series means traffic didn't reach that stage (ADR §7), e.g. cache hits skip upstreamwait; interceptor rates count invocations, not requests.
panels.title: Per-stage throughput (samples/s)

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). channelRead to just before ACL. Records even on ACL denial (ADR §7 #1).
panels.title: T0→T1 request.preprocess

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). ACL lookup. Zero is normal for superuser/ACL-disabled requests (ADR §7 #1).
panels.title: T1→T2 request.authorization

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). API-specific request rebuild. Skipped on cache hit and on all-topics-blocked produce (ADR §7 #2, #9).
panels.title: T3→T4 request.rebuilder

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). Rebuilt request waiting for broker/channel then sent to Kafka wire.
panels.title: T4→T5 request.upstreamqueue

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). Kafka round-trip — the one stage where P99 is directly meaningful. Skipped on acks=0 and on upstream timeout (ADR §7 #5, #6).
panels.title: T5→T6 request.upstreamwait

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). API-specific response rebuild. Skipped on cache hit (ADR §7 #9).
panels.title: T6→T7 response.rebuilder

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). Response ACL lookup.
panels.title: T8→T9 response.authorization

panels.description: Mean and max are exact; P99 reads flat inside the first bucket (1ms) until this stage degrades (ADR §4). Serialize + hop to event loop + head-of-line wait + socket write. A spike usually means head-of-line blocking behind a slow earlier request on the same connection, not a slow client (ADR §1). Not a delivery signal.
panels.title: T9→T10 response.send

title: Conduktor Gateway Lifecycle
